svg.text: NEXUS-OPS: ECG DATA PROCESSING, VALIDATION & QUANTUM-CLASSICAL EVALUATION
End-to-End Scientific Architecture: From MIT-BIH Acquisition to 6-Qubit VQC & Classical ML Benchmarking

g.text: 200 ms & 600 ms baseline removal; 0.5–40 Hz filter
Pre-R: 144 samples (400 ms) | Post-R: 216 samples (600 ms)

svg.text: EXPLICIT RECORD-LEVEL DATA PARTITIONING (LORO PROTOCOL A)

g.text: Record 106: 100 beats (50 N, 50 V) | Record 119: 100 beats (50 N, 50 V)
Role: Benchmark Scaler Fitted on Both Records (106 & 119) | LORO Model Selection
Record 200: 50 beats (25 N, 25 V) | Record 208: 50 beats (25 N, 25 V)
Role: Quarantined Single-Pass Evaluation Under Frozen Parameters

svg.text: Enforces strict record-level separation (independent recording streams, not verified patient identities)

g.text: Zero record overlap across splits verified (src/classical_baseline_audit.py)

svg.text: Extraction Module: src/feature_extraction.py | Yields: features_train.csv (200x6) & features_test.csv (100x6)
Latency note: post_rr requires observing succeeding beat, introducing a 1-beat retrospective processing latency

g.text: Standard normalization fitted strictly on Development Cohort (N = 200)
L2 penalty (C=1.0), liblinear solver, balanced weights
RBF kernel (C=1.0, scale gamma), probability calibration
100 trees, max depth 5, balanced class weighting
Confusion Matrix (LR): TN=42, FP=8, FN=0, TP=50 | F1-Macro: 0.92
Interpretability: Pre-RR & QRS Duration deliver highest predictive weight
• Linear/logistic boundary separates morphological ECG features effectively.
• 100% Sensitivity on VEBs: Zero missed ventricular ectopic beats.
• High Specificity (84%): Low false positive rate on normal sinus beats.
• Establishes the classical reference baseline (92%) for comparison.
• No hyperparameter tuning performed on held-out test cohort.

svg.text: TRACK B: QUANTUM ML (6-QUBIT VQC PIPELINE)

g.text: Fitted on Full Development Cohort: Records 106 & 119 (N = 200)
Linearly maps 6 features to [0, pi] rotational angles for single-qubit Ry encoding
Validation limitation: Benchmark scaler incorporates Record 119, not Record 106 alone
Test records 200 & 208 strictly quarantined; clamped to [0, pi] (src/feature_scaling.py)
Selected Checkpoint: fold_1_seed_303 (Frozen Parameter Vector theta*)
Val Score = 0.9592 | Val MSE = 0.1020 | Val Acc = 100% | Optimal 12 theta frozen
6 single-qubit Ry(x_i) rotations (x_0 ... x_5 in [0, pi])
Quarantined Records 200 & 208 under Frozen Parameters theta* (src/vqc_evaluation.py)
Confusion Matrix: TN=26, FP=24, FN=0, TP=50 | F1-Score: 0.806 | MSE Loss: 0.1626
Held-out benchmark: 100% sensitivity on 50/50 VEB samples (zero false negatives)
Specificity limit (52%): Modest specificity reflects baseline shift on held-out records
The VQC matches the classical baseline's sensitivity on this test set, but has lower accuracy and specificity.
Capacity Limit: 6-Qubit VQC exceeds 5 physical qubits
• The selected six-qubit encoding cannot be directly mapped to this five-qubit target.
• Possible redesign options include circuit cutting, feature reduction (to 5),
Processor B: 9-Qubit Simulated Heavy-Hex-Inspired Tree (Primary Target)
Transpilation Results (Simulation Only, Not a Physical QPU Execution)
Transpiled Metrics: Circuit Depth = 15 | CX Gates = 5 | SWAP Gates = 0
• Simulated mapping to physical path [0-1-2-4-5-6] requires 0 SWAPs
• Zero routing overhead: Linear CX ansatz connectivity matches tree sub-path
• Enforces strict record-level separation between training
• Patient-level separation has not been verified.
• Preserves scientific honesty regarding external generalization.
All performance claims are strictly scoped to record-level splits.
• All quantum simulations conducted on Qiskit Aer 0.17.2.
• Uses noiseless statevector & noisy depolarizing shots.
• NO physical quantum processing unit (QPU) execution claimed.
• Transpilation metrics represent compile-time routing models.
Hardware noise simulated via depolarizing + readout models.
• This project is an exploratory NISQ feasibility benchmark.
• NO claim of quantum advantage or supremacy is made.
• Classical Logistic Regression achieves higher accuracy (92% vs 76%).
• The VQC matches the classical baseline's sensitivity on
this test set, but has lower accuracy and specificity.
